deities: Peddamma Thalli (Goddess of the Mother Goddess; worshipped as Santhana Lakshmi and as Mahishasura Mardini, eight-armed, Simha vahini)
festivals: Bonalu (Ashada Masam, June-July) - the temple's main festival; women carry decorated earthen pots with rice, jaggery, milk and curd as offerings

history.period: Modern - shrine dates back over a century (established 1908 per one account / more than 150 years per another); idol re-consecrated by Hampi Virupaksha Peetham pontiffs in 1984; Rajagopuram built 1993; five-storey sanctum and seven-storey Rajagopuram renovated under the late ex-minister P. Janardhan Reddy
history.summary: The best-supported referent for CSV row 983 is the famous Sri Peddamma Thalli Temple (Peddamma Gudi) at Road No. 55, CBI Colony, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad - the best-known Peddamma temple and a major Bonalu centre in the twin cities. Legend says the Jubilee Hills area was once a dense uninhabited forest; shepherds and farmers worshipped a small idol of the Goddess under a rock, and after the Goddess (in one telling) slayed the Asura she came here to quench her thirst at a well where a shepherd later found her idol. The humble shrine (established 1908 in a hut per one account; more than 150 years old per others) grew as Jubilee Hills developed into a residential hub in the 1990s, especially under the late P. Janardhan Reddy (PJR), and the Rajagopuram was built in 1993 with a five-storey sanctum and seven-storey gopuram in Dravidian style. Sources conflict on the exact origin date (1908 vs 150+ years) - flag as (verify). The presiding deity is 'Peddamma' ('mother of mothers'), worshipped as Santhana Lakshmi seated on a lion in one tradition and as the eight-armed Mahishasura Mardini in another. A popular belief holds that a one-rupee coin standing upright at the base of the Dhvajasthambham signifies a granted wish. CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV town 'Secunderabad' is an error - the temple is in JUBILEE HILLS, HYDERABAD (about 12-15 km from Secunderabad). Corrected.
